examples.ko: 우리 팀은 위기에 더 강하게 결속했어요.
examples.en: Our team pulled together more strongly in the crisis.
The citizens united as one and protected the village.

examples.ko: 회원들이 결속하면 큰 힘이 될 거예요.
examples.en: If the members unite, it will be a great strength.

examples.ko: 함께 고생한 일이 우리를 결속하게 했어요.
examples.en: Going through hard times together bound us closer.
The staff went to a workshop on the weekend to bond as a team.
The small countries promised to unite with one another.

explain: 사람들이 한마음으로 단단히 뭉칠 때 써요. 일상에서는 '뭉치다'가 더 자연스럽고, '결속하다'는 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 명사로 '결속을 다지다', '결속력'이라는 표현도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when people firmly come together as one. In daily talk '뭉치다' sounds more natural, while '결속하다' shows up more in writing and the news. The noun forms '결속을 다지다' and '결속력' are also common.

examples.en: When the crisis came, the villagers stood together.

examples.ko: 팀이 단결하면 어려운 일도 해낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the team unites, it can accomplish even hard things.
Everyone came together and cheered for our team.
The students joined forces and gave their opinion to the school.
It was really nice to see them stand together.
We will keep standing together as one.

explain: 많은 사람이 한마음으로 힘을 모으는 거예요. 팀, 노동자, 국민처럼 큰 집단에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '뭉치다'가 더 편하고, '다 같이 뭉치자'처럼 말해요. '협력하다'는 일을 함께 하는 것이고, 단결하다는 마음과 힘이 하나가 되는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: It means many people putting their strength together with one mind. It suits large groups such as a team, workers, or a nation. In casual talk '뭉치다' is easier, as in '다 같이 뭉치자'. '협력하다' is working on something together, while 단결하다 is about hearts and strength becoming one.

examples.en: My mother raised and supported three children on her own.
My parents supported me throughout my life studying abroad.

examples.ko: 남편 공부를 뒷바라지하느라 일을 쉬지 못했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't take a break from work because I was supporting my husband's studies.
Looking after a child's needs isn't easy.
The family who supported the athlete shed tears.
I'd like to support them, but I don't have much money to spare.

explain: 자식이나 가족의 공부, 일을 곁에서 돈과 정성으로 돕는 것을 말해요. 그냥 '돕다'보다 오랫동안 생활 전체를 챙기며 희생한다는 느낌이 있어요. 비슷하게 생긴 '뒷받침하다'는 의견이나 계획을 돕는 데도 써요.
explain_en: It means helping a child or family member's studies or work from behind with money and care. Compared with plain '돕다', it suggests long-term sacrifice and looking after their whole life. The similar-looking '뒷받침하다' can also support opinions or plans.

examples.en: I will surely repay your kindness.
I want to repay my parents' love.

examples.ko: 저는 선생님의 기대에 보답하려고 열심히 공부해요.
examples.en: I study hard to live up to my teacher's expectations.
How should I repay their kindness?

examples.ko: 그 선수는 팬들의 응원에 우승으로 보답했어요.
examples.en: The player repaid the fans' support with a championship.
I bought dinner as a way of saying thanks.

explain: 받은 도움이나 기대에 행동으로 돌려줄 때 써요. '갚다'는 빌린 돈에도 쓰지만 '보답하다'는 감사의 마음이 담긴 점잖은 말이에요. '은혜에', '기대에', '응원에'처럼 '~에'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you give back, through action, for help or expectations you received. '갚다' also covers borrowed money, but '보답하다' is a more dignified word full of gratitude. It takes '~에', as in '은혜에', '기대에', '응원에'.

examples.en: He supports his parents and younger sibling on his own.

examples.ko: 가족을 부양하려고 두 가지 일을 해요.
examples.en: I work two jobs to support my family.

examples.ko: 정부는 경기를 부양하기 위해 대책을 내놓았어요.
examples.en: The government put out measures to stimulate the economy.

examples.ko: 아들이 나이 드신 어머니를 부양하고 있어요.
examples.en: The son is taking care of his elderly mother financially.
I have many family members to support, so my salary falls short.
My older sister kept supporting our parents even after she married.

explain: 돈을 벌어서 부모나 아이 같은 가족을 먹여 살리는 거예요. 일상에서는 '먹여 살리다'라고도 해요. '키우다'는 아이를 기르는 것이고, 부양하다는 생활비를 책임진다는 쪽이에요. 뉴스에서 '경기 부양'이라고 하면 경제를 일으켜 세운다는 쪽으로 써요.
explain_en: It means earning money to support family such as parents or children. In daily talk people also say '먹여 살리다'. '키우다' is raising a child, while 부양하다 is about taking responsibility for living costs. In the news, '경기 부양' means boosting the economy.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 팬들에게 멋진 공연을 선사해요.
examples.en: This singer gives her fans a wonderful performance.
I want to treat my parents to a family trip.
An event giving books to children was held.

examples.ko: 큰 웃음을 선사하는 영화라서 자주 봐요.
examples.en: It's a movie that gives you big laughs, so I watch it often.
I secretly prepared a surprise party to give them.

examples.ko: 새해에 회사가 직원들에게 특별 휴가를 선사할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will give its employees special time off for the new year.

explain: '주다'보다 격식 있고 멋진 느낌이라, 선물보다 공연·웃음·감동처럼 기쁜 경험을 줄 때 잘 어울려요. 사람에게 물건을 건넬 때는 '드리다'나 '주다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: More formal and polished than 주다. It fits giving a joyful experience such as a performance, laughter or emotion more than handing over an object. For everyday gifts, 주다 or 드리다 sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 그 의사는 환자에 대한 인간애가 깊어요.
examples.en: That doctor has deep love for humanity toward his patients.

examples.ko: 인간애를 담은 영화를 보고 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried watching a film full of humanity.

examples.ko: 재난 현장에서 인간애를 보여 준 사람들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people showed compassion at the disaster site.
It's a volunteer activity that began out of love for humanity.

examples.ko: 작가는 인간애로 가득한 시를 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: The writer wrote many poems full of love for people.
A society without humanity feels cold.

explain: 특정한 한 사람이 아니라 '사람 전체'를 향한 따뜻한 마음이에요. '박애'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 말이고, 문학이나 뉴스에서 '인간애가 넘치다'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is warm feeling toward people in general rather than one specific person. It resembles '박애' (philanthropy), which is stiffer. In literature and news you see phrases like '인간애가 넘치다'.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 친선 경기를 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two countries agreed to play a friendly match.
The purpose of this meeting is goodwill.
It was a friendly tournament, so I enjoyed it without pressure.

examples.ko: 두 학교는 올해부터 친선 교류를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The two schools started a goodwill exchange this year.

examples.ko: 친선 방문으로 도시를 찾은 대표단을 환영했어요.
examples.en: We welcomed the delegation visiting the city on a goodwill trip.
The mayor strengthened ties with the sister city.

explain: '친선 경기', '친선 방문', '친선 대회'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 이기고 지는 것보다 사이를 좋게 하는 게 목적일 때 써서, 우승을 다투는 정식 경기와 달라요. 친구 사이에는 '친하다'를 쓰고, 친선은 나라·학교·단체 사이에 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used before another noun, as in '친선 경기', '친선 방문' and '친선 대회'. It points to improving relations rather than winning, which sets it apart from an official match. Between friends you say '친하다'; 친선 suits countries, schools and organizations.
